target: Existing Capacity duality, certified optimization and tensor regularization manuscript
purpose: Own synthesis for defensible intake and eventual knowledge-tree integration; no new theorem, paper or graph confidence promotion

levels.formal: No newly checked proof-assistant result. Rational certificate acceptance is exact finite arithmetic, not a formal proof of all source theorems.
levels.literature: Current frozen manuscript claims and cited prior results, with exact-source/report boundaries; the current scope review is still pending.
levels.heuristic: Statement-level distinctness from the Sharpness predecessor supports treating the manuscript as a substantive sequel, pending ordinary case reconciliation. It does not certify worldwide priority.
levels.speculative: No general efficient small finite determinant-witness construction follows from capacity-value approximation; abandon any such inference without a separate theorem.

claims.source: Theorem1, equation dual; Lemmas fixed and convex
claims.mechanism: For each covariance, determinant-one scaling gives a continuous linear Gram pairing. Polar/geodesic interpolation makes the Loewner upper image convex. Sion exchanges compact covariance maximization and the convex upper-image infimum.
claims.hypothesis_eliminated: No need for a false ordinary convexity assumption on SL(d,C)^2, nor attainment of its scaling infimum.
claims.limits: Uses classical minimax; not a new general minimax theorem. Complex covariance conventions must stay consistent.
claims.falsifier: A complex tuple/covariance violating the trace-pairing identity, or endpoint scalings violating Loewner convex interpolation, defeats the argument.

claims.claim: Optimized-capacity tensor multiplicativity, including entangled joint covariance
claims.mechanism: Known fixed-map capacity multiplicativity and product covariances give the lower bound. The Gram dual permits product scalings and the largest-eigenvalue product rule to bound every joint covariance from above.
claims.hypothesis_eliminated: No product/separability restriction on the maximizing covariance is imposed in the conclusion.
claims.limits: Fixed-map multiplicativity is an explicit external theorem. Zero factors require the epsilon-to-infimum argument, not minimizer existence.
claims.falsifier: A tuple pair with an exact certified joint-covariance lower value exceeding the separate dual upper witnesses would contradict the claimed optimized identity.

claims.claim: Tensor-regularized amplified determinant equals optimized capacity
claims.mechanism: Apply the earlier universal C/e comparison once to the tensor-power tuple and use optimized-capacity multiplicativity, then take the nth root.
claims.hypothesis_eliminated: No interchange of auxiliary-amplification supremum and tensor limit, and no uniform auxiliary witness-size estimate is used.
claims.retained_hypothesis: Earlier universal comparison ARR-2026-1DGGW5KX2M9R4VJT v1; not independently re-audited by this context review.
claims.limits: This short consequence stays inside the substantive duality/optimization paper; not a separate paper. Dimension of direct tensor evaluation still grows exponentially.
claims.falsifier: Failure of the cited universal comparison would remove this identification while leaving the stated duality/optimization core logically separable.

claims.claim: Finite-bit value/covariance approximation and rational value certificates
claims.source: Finite-bit section and certificate sections; existing retained exact examples
claims.mechanism: Published fixed-map scaling oracle plus rational cutting-plane reduction, positive feasible center and explicit precision budgets. Rational Gram witnesses bracket the value by exact matrix arithmetic.
claims.hypothesis_eliminated: Certification of selected finite output values need not trust a floating-point search as its acceptance oracle.
claims.limits: General M1/GLS implementation and benchmarks are absent. Existing finite certificate examples do not prove the full complexity theorem or construct general finite determinant witnesses.
claims.falsifier: A malformed or false rational certificate accepted by the exact checker, or a hidden precision/feasible-center hypothesis in the reduction, is a material objection; preserved negative-control evidence must remain available.

deduplication: The existing Sharpness theorem constructs tuples approaching the universal factor e. This manuscript must cite that result and retain its distinct construction scope; it must not sell the same factor-e optimality as a new current result.
